title: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls (regio)
heading: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls
requires: Storyguide-placed site in the Black Forest (never found)
summary: A forest-spirit regio whose levels are the seven waterfalls; a visitor may only ascend each level by completing a different Quest, gaining a new level of understanding of the Forest at each step. Gives the spirit's Might, traits and powers as a stat block.
quotes: **Magic Might:** 50
Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker), Guide, Oath-Swearing, Regio, Shroud
related: Realms and Forest Paths in the Rhine Tribunal

title: Studying in the Great Library (Durenmar)
heading: STUDYING IN THE GREAT LIBRARY
requires: Visit to Durenmar (members and House Bonisagus exempt)
summary: Visiting magi earn seasons of study credit at the Great Library by contributing tomes, new spells or a season of copying, or by paying vis; rules cover priority when two magi want the same tome, certamen to settle disputes, and limits on removing or copying books.
quotes: For each new contribution to the Great Library, a magus is permitted to study freely there for two seasons.
a magus may instead gain a single season of credit by volunteering for a season of copying
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bonisagus)

title: Searching the Great Library: lab notes, spells, tractatus and summae
heading: THE CONTENTS OF THE GREAT LIBRARY
summary: Floor-by-floor procedures for finding a desired item in the Great Library: Intelligence + Magic Theory to locate lab notes, a stress die against an Ease Factor to find a Lab Text, and simple-die rolls (with Durenmar Lore and rank bonuses) to find tractatus and summae and to set their Quality.
quotes: The success should be determined by an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against an appropriate Ease Factor.
The Ease Factor for standard spells is 3, or 6 for a specific version of a general-level standard spell up to level 40.
To determine the Quality of a studied tractatus, roll a simple die and add 2.
To determine whether a summa of a specified Art is available to a magus, roll a simple die and add 10.

title: Durenmar covenfolk: Warping from the strong Magic aura
heading: Covenfolk
requires: Covenfolk of Durenmar (covenant in a strong Magic aura)
summary: Durenmar's servants and grogs are shaped by life in a strong Magic aura: each has Warping-derived Minor Flaws, and the very old gain a Supernatural Ability Virtue. A model for generating covenfolk of any covenant that lives in a strong aura.
quotes: All covenfolk have at least one Minor Flaw due to Warping, and those over 30 years old have two.

title: The Fane of the Founders
heading: The Fane of the Founders
summary: A hidden glade with a Magic aura in which twelve magi renew the Oath of the Founders every seven years; the stone is treated as an artifact with Magic Might and a limited set of forest powers, and it yields vis to those who perform the rite.
quotes: Thus, the Fane may be treated as if it has a Magic Might of 40
Produce Vis, Shroud, Oath-Swearing, Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker; temporarily)
related: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls

title: The Source of the Danube (Faerie regio)
heading: The Source of the Danube
requires: Storyguide-placed site in the eastern Black Forest
summary: An enchanted spring and bottomless pool with a Faerie aura that rises within the water and in the deeper levels of a regio, ending in a gateway to Arcadia; large amounts of Aquam vis can be harvested at the cost of angering the river spirit.
quotes: There is a Faerie aura of 3 in the region of the pool, which rises to 5 if one is within the water itself.

title: The Rottweiler (playable dog grog)
heading: The Rottweiler
requires: Storyguide approval; a magus who keeps Rottweilers
summary: Optional rules for playing a faerie-blooded hunting dog as a grog: it uses Cunning in place of Intelligence, receives a fixed package of Virtues and Flaws, and has its age and aging rolls scaled to dog years. Some have faerie blood that slows aging or grants Second Sight.
quotes: the hound may be created as a normal character, except that it has Cunning instead of Intelligence
Their bite has the same combat statistics as a dagger.
Calculate their age (and experience) as for a human, and use this age for making aging rolls

title: The Magestones of Verditius (portable Magic aura)
heading: The Magestones of Verditius
requires: Possession of a magestone (Durenmar and Oculus Septentrionalis hold them)
summary: Rare Creo Vim artifacts that each project a small Magic aura, allowing a covenant with no natural aura to give its magi lab work in a Magic aura for a limited number of seasons a year; Hermetic theory cannot replicate them.
quotes: Each stone manifests a Magic aura of 3, large enough to cover a large room or laboratory.
so that they are able to work in a Magic aura in their labs for up to two seasons every year

title: The Holy Vehm (secret courts of northern Germany)
heading: The Holy Vehm
summary: Describes how the secret Vehmic courts try capital crimes: who may be a member and who is exempt, the officials, how a summons works, and how many witnesses are needed for proof or acquittal. Useful for running a Vehm trial or hunt against suspected hedge wizards.
quotes: his accuser can present to the court seven witnesses to his own character as a man to be trusted
he requires twenty-one witnesses in favor of innocence to assure his acquittal
related: Order of Hermes and mundane law

title: The Brocken: Faerie aura that doubles on Walpurgis Night
heading: The Brocken
requires: Visit to the Brocken in the Harz
summary: A potent supernatural mountain where the Faerie aura varies by altitude and doubles on Walpurgis Night; also a source of a vis plant, a vision-granting spring and a place to find potential apprentices.
quotes: The lower slopes of the Brocken have a Faerie aura of 2, with 4 at the summit. These values are doubled on Walpurgis Night.

title: Fengheld's Chapter Houses (covenant chapter rules)
heading: Fengheld's Chapter Houses
requires: A covenant that has founded chapter houses
summary: Explains how a covenant can be spread over several sites as chapter houses: all chapters remain part of the main covenant, share its charter and Tribunal rulings, and may add a local charter for their own residents. The sidebar also suggests how a player covenant can become one of the chapters.
quotes: All magi must accept the charter of Fengheld, and any strictures or rulings from the Tribunal that apply to Fengheld also apply to the chapter houses (and vice versa).
a chapter usually has a local charter that applies only to those magi who live in the chapter house

title: The Feengrotten (shifting caves yielding Imaginem vis)
heading: The Feengrotten
summary: A faerie-touched cave network with a weak Magic aura whose passages shift; only those who are genuinely lost for days emerge covered in Imaginem vis dust, while anyone trying to exploit the property gets plain dust.
quotes: The Feengrotten has a Magic aura of 1.
the dust is Imaginem vis, the quantity dependent on how many days that they were lost

title: Crintera's four-level heartbeast regio
heading: Setting and Physical Description
requires: Visiting Crintera (the House Bjornaer domus magna on Rugen)
summary: Crintera lies in a four-level regio whose auras rise by level; as each boundary is crossed every visitor must resist a Corpus effect that brings out a heartbeast, first changing Personality Traits and then causing minor physical changes. Parma Magica and a Bjornaer Heartbeast roll can resist or shrug off the changes.
quotes: There are four levels to the magical regio, with auras of 1, 3, 5, and 8.
every character must resist a Corpus effect with a Penetration Total equal to the Ease Factor needed to see the next level
Of course, magi of House Bjornaer can shrug off these changes with a Heartbeast roll, should they want to.

title: The Gathering of Twelve Years (House Bjornaer)
heading: The Gathering of Twelve Years
summary: The House Bjornaer assembly held at Crintera every twelve years, when most initiations into the House's Mysteries take place. Includes advice for running the Gathering in a saga, including giving non-Bjornaer players a Bjornaer character for the event.
quotes: most initiations into the Mysteries of House Bjornaer are conducted during the gathering
The next gathering, due in 1227, is likely to be politically explosive
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

title: Council of Elders and the Seats of Crintera (Bjornaer governance)
heading: Culture and Traditions
summary: How the Council of Elders of Crintera is organized: six seats with fixed duties, how vacant seats are filled at the Gathering, the Primus's Seat of the Wolf, the reserved Senior Elder seat and its casting vote.
quotes: When an Elder dies or passes into Final Twilight, he will not be replaced until the next Gathering of Twelve Years.
The Senior Elder has the casting vote in any decision of the council
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

title: Durenmar guest laboratories and vis fees
heading: THE TOWER OF NOTATUS
summary: Describes the fee in vis a covenant may charge a visiting magus of suitable rank for a season in its guest laboratories, with a cheaper rate for the small standard labs; a model for pricing guest lab use.
quotes: albeit with a charge of at least five pawns of vis
for the lesser fee of two pawns of vis per season each

title: Crintera covenfolk: the six animal clans
heading: Covenfolk
requires: Covenant of House Bjornaer (Crintera) or a similar heartbeast-themed turb
summary: Organizes the grogs and covenfolk of Crintera into six animal clans mirroring the Elders' seats, each with a role, preferred weapons and a clan leader; shows how to build a themed turb whose warriors share a heartbeast style.
quotes: The grogs and covenfolk are divided into six clans, named just as the six seats of the Elders.

title: Pomeranian werewolves (skinchanger families)
heading: The Werewolves of Pomerania
requires: Born into a Pomeranian werewolf family (storyguide approval)
summary: Explains how shapeshifting is inherited in Pomeranian werewolf families, which Virtue or Flaw a child receives, how animals react to them, and offers a list of suitable additional Virtues and Flaws for playing a werewolf companion.
quotes: A child born into a werewolf family will acquire the Skinchanger Virtue.
Those unlucky enough to be born into human families will usually acquire the Lycanthrope Flaw, and be unable to control their change.

title: Slave trade and prices
heading: The Slave Trade
summary: Describes the Prague slave market, who controls it, and gives a rule of thumb for what a slave costs relative to a horse, with higher prices for skilled, strong or young slaves.
quotes: An unremarkable slave may be purchased for as little as a few schillings
the younger, healthier, and stronger the slave is, the more he or she may be sold for
